 Advertisement OU coach Brent Venables questions why Ole Miss couldn't drive to Norman after FAA's ground stoppage
 Advertisement Updated: 9:27 AM CST Nov 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Dacoda Wahpekeche Reporter OU coach Brent Venables questions why Ole Miss couldn't drive to Norman after FAA's ground stoppage
 Updated: 9:27 AM CST Nov 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Dacoda Wahpekeche Reporter NORMAN, Okla. — College football saw some controversy over the weekend as the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stoppage order disrupted travel plans for several programs over the weekend. 
 One of the impacted programs was the Ole Miss football team, which did not make its planned trip to Norman on Friday to play the Sooners for their slated Saturday afternoon game. The Rebels did not travel to Oklahoma until Saturday, forcing the game to be pushed back to Sunday. 
 Advertisement 'Absolutely wrong': Bob Stoops calls out SEC's decision to postpone OU-Ole Miss game to Sunday The Oklahoma-Ole Miss game was the only one in all of college football to be played on Sunday. 
 Ole Miss wasn't in the air when the nationwide ground stop was ordered. University officials, however, said issues arose with their flight crew's duty time even after the order was lifted. 
 >> Video Below: Mateer accounts for 181 yards of offense and Oklahoma holds on to beat No. 19 Mississippi 24-17 
 SEC and Ole Miss leadership said every avenue to get the Rebels to Norman was explored, but it seems OU leadership doubted that. Oklahoma Athletics Director Roger Denny said the SEC even told the Sooners they would have to forfeit the game if they did not play on Sunday. 
 Sooner players and coaches called the travel delays and playing on Sunday "disappointing" and "weird." 
 Oklahoma beat Ole Miss 24-17 , and Brent Venables said during the postgame news conference that he wondered why the Rebels couldn't have just driven the eight hours from Oxford to Norman. Venables added that he was disappointed for Sooner Nation. 
 "People plan their whole year, their calendar year around Sooner football. That's very real financially. Time off, all those things (with) our home schedule," Venables said. "Our merchants locally, I feel terrible for our local merchants. There's no recovery, if you will. You can't get that back when we only play six home games." 
 >> Video Below: Norman church keeps Sunday Mass schedule despite OU-Ole Miss game rescheduling 
 The Sooners' head football coach said his team tried blocking out the noise on Saturday by going to the movies and spending some time with their families. 
 Moving the game to Sunday had major impacts on the Norman community, as some churches closed and others moved their service times around. 
 The Sooners' next game against Texas A&M was initially scheduled for 11 a.m. on Saturday. That game has now been pushed back to 2:45 p.m.
